mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which boosts corporate profit margins and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of six consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months indicates a broad-based demand collapse, which increases recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a rapidly tightening labor market that boosts wage inflation and compresses profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during months with PAYEMS above 12-month moving average and concurrent UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 1% for an extended period (six months or more) in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 1.0% for at least 6 months AND CPIAUCSL < 2.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS <= 1.0% for six months and CPIAUCSL < 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio above its 10-year average) alongside a decline in consumption expenditures (GDPC1) indicates precautionary behavior and weakening demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio > 10-year average AND GDPC1 declines for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio exceeds its 10-year average and GDPC1 declines for three months.
